title: Prefix Sums
summary: Precompute running totals so the sum of any contiguous range is one subtraction.
lesson:
How it works
- `prefix[i]` is the sum of the first `i` elements, with `prefix[0] = 0`.
- The sum of the range from `i` up to but not including `j` is `prefix[j] - prefix[i]`.
- Building the prefixes takes `O(n)`; each later range query takes `O(1)`.

When to reach for it
- Many questions about range sums over an array that does not change.
- Counting or finding subarrays whose sum meets a condition, including inputs with negative numbers.
- Two-dimensional grids: a 2D prefix table answers rectangle sums the same way.

Common patterns
- Range query: answer each query by subtracting two prefixes.
- Prefix plus hash map: count earlier prefixes that differ from the current one by the target.
- Difference arrays: the inverse idea, applying many range updates then taking one prefix pass.

Pitfalls
- Forgetting the empty prefix of zero, which drops subarrays that start at index 0.
- Integer overflow on large inputs; use `long` when sums can exceed `int`.
- Off-by-one between inclusive and exclusive range ends.
